svg.title: Front view muscle chart. Primary muscles: Chest. Secondary muscles: Front Delts, Triceps.
Back view muscle chart. Primary muscles: Chest. Secondary muscles: Front Delts, Triceps.

svg.text: It carries the heaviest load of the three while the bench does the balancing for you, so the chest gets pushed hard
and then progressed in small, repeatable jumps for years.
Bouncing the bar off your chest — it dumps the tension the pecs should be absorbing and drives the load straight
Flaring the elbows out to a flat 90° — it jams the head of the humerus into the front of the shoulder, which is the
Letting the heels lift and the hips come off the bench — you lose leg drive and turn a chest press into a
Lie flat, eyes under the bar, feet planted and shoulder blades pinched
back. Unrack and lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows at about 45°. Drive
the bar up and slightly back over the shoulders without bouncing.
Breathing — Fill your chest and brace at lockout, inhale as the bar descends to
mid-chest, then exhale hard through the press back up.
Coach's cue — Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and never flare elbows
Use a spotter, or set the rack pins a couple of centimetres below your
chest height so a failed rep lands on steel instead of your throat.
Rehearse the unrack path before you load up and end the set the moment the
bar stalls or the elbows collapse inward; if a shoulder impingement or
AC-joint injury is still symptomatic, press dumbbells on a slight incline

Best on paper is not always best for you. Which exercise builds a body part fastest depends on your build, your injury history and how much of the movement you already own — someone who cannot yet hold

a flat back under load will get more from the exercise ranked third than from the one ranked first. Treat this as a starting point for a conversation, not a verdict: ask a coach on the floor before you
